processes.name: Compare two equivalent writings of one model; decide which shows the vertex; verify by algebra and by table/graph
Inspect vertex form: vertex (h, k) including plus-inside, axis x = h, maximum or minimum from the sign of a
Predict what changing one of a, h, or k will do, then check the graph and the rewritten equation
Expand vertex form into standard form and verify equivalent representations with graphing technology
Describe what can be read from vertex form compared with standard form and factored form, without producing those other writings

candidates.title: Fountain arc: which writing shows the peak (dual path)
candidates.purpose: Decision hook with two equivalent models plus algebra and table/graph paths. Original wording; consistent with fountain opener. Not a commercial stem.

candidates.title: Vertex of y = −2(x + 3)^2 + 5 (h-sign)
candidates.purpose: Extra plus-inside vertex reading if a licence exists; use part (d) only. The full bank item also asks for a transformation list (A2.5/A2.6), which is not this lesson.
candidates.exclusion_reason: Unknown commercial licence (Nelson Functions 11 local bank). Do not print the bank stem in student HTML.

candidates.title: Predict vertex of (x + 3)^2 + 1, then check sliders
candidates.purpose: Partial support for plus-inside inspection: name the vertex before any slider moves, then check on the local board (GeoGebra is analogue only; do not require it). The same board then carries predict–move–check for one parameter.

candidates.title: Ministry A2.6 sample: vertex of −2(x + 1)^2
candidates.purpose: Varied second inspection: plus-inside with k = 0 so maximum versus minimum cannot be taken from k, and a < 0. Quote the seed sample; do not treat sketching-by-transformation as a new M4 target.

candidates.title: OpenStax worked reading: y = −3(x + 2)^2 + 4
candidates.purpose: Fully explained first inspection: match (x + 2) to (x − h), name vertex, axis, and maximum from the sign of a. Keep OpenStax wording in the source field; Ontario name is vertex form.

candidates.title: MCF3M A2.7 sample: expand 3(x − 1)^2 + 4
candidates.purpose: Independent expand-and-verify after a worked expansion. Verbatim Ministry sample. Seed has no key; do not invent expanded coefficients.

candidates.title: OpenStax: expand ½(x + 2)^2 − 3 and check a table
candidates.purpose: Fully explained expansion of vertex form, then table check that both writings give the same outputs. Same catalogue record as the inspection reading; this is the Figure 7 expand path only.

candidates.title: OpenStax verbal: advantage of this form
candidates.purpose: Independent verbal contrast: what vertex form makes readable versus ax^2 + bx + c. Do not ask students to produce another writing. Copywriter must not call a(x − h)^2 + k “standard form” in student prose.

candidates.title: Nelson: label vertex and axis from mixed equations
candidates.purpose: Further vertex and axis labelling on vertex-form equations if a licence exists. Skip the standard-form part (vertex not readable by inspection; completing the square is Lesson 2).
candidates.exclusion_reason: Unknown commercial licence (Nelson Functions 11 local bank). Do not print the bank stem in student HTML.

candidates.title: OpenStax §5.1 ex. 22: domain and range of −2(x + 3)^2 − 6
candidates.purpose: Later retrieval of plus-inside inspection via domain and range from k and the sign of a. Catalogue has no solution element; do not invent the range. Not yet its own catalogue record.

candidates.title: Which form for which information (A2.10)
candidates.purpose: Further three-form contrast if a licence exists: which writing for vertex, intercepts, zeros, axis, domain and range. Use only the readable prompt; ignore garbled OCR.
candidates.exclusion_reason: Unknown commercial licence (Nelson Functions 11 local bank). Do not print the bank stem in student HTML.

candidates.title: OpenStax §5.1 ex. 53: family (x − 2)^2, (x − 3)^2, (x + 4)^2
candidates.purpose: Independent try-another for one-parameter change in h, including plus-inside versus minus-inside. Catalogue has no solution element; do not invent a key. Not yet its own catalogue record.

candidates.title: MathNet 0gz2 (olympiad; rewrite required)
candidates.purpose: Olympiad packing and difficulty; not an MCF3M worksheet. Contest stem is not classroom copy. Rewrite was not accepted for this lesson.
candidates.exclusion_reason: Excessive difficulty (Ukraine olympiad). Licence not confirmed for classroom use of the contest text; MathNet convenience key is unverified. Do not print the contest stem.
